content:
Here’s an advanced and completely different Keras project—far beyond conventional CNN or segmentation work—using fine‑grained visual recognition with a Navigator‑Teacher‑Scrutinizer (NTS‑Net) architecture for bird species classification on the CUB‑200‑2011 dataset.

Project Title

ai-ml-ds-KjXz9MqYgA – Fine‑Grained Bird Species Classifier via NTS‑Net
fine_grained_bird_ntsnet.py

📝 Short Description

Implement an end‑to‑end Keras v2 NTS‑Net: navigator proposes candidate regions, teacher scores them, scrutinizer combines global+local evidence to classify among 200 bird species.

# fine_grained_bird_ntsnet.py

import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers
import tensorflow_datasets as tfds
import numpy as np

# NOTE: For clarity, runtime shortcuts & key modules only. Production code would modularize further.

# === Config & Hyperparams ===
img_size: tuple = (224, 224)
topN: int = 4
num_classes: int = 200
batch_size: int = 16
epochs: int = 50
learning_rate: float = 1e-4

# === Load CUB-200-2011 via TFDS ===
(ds_train, ds_test), ds_info = tfds.load('caltech_birds2011', split=['train','test'], with_info=True, as_supervised=True)

def preprocess(image: tf.Tensor, label: tf.Tensor):
    image = tf.image.resize(image, img_size)
    image = image / 255.0
    return image, label

ds_train = ds_train.map(preprocess).batch(batch_size).prefetch(4)
ds_test = ds_test.map(preprocess).batch(batch_size).prefetch(4)

# === Backbone Feature Extractor ===
base_cnn = keras.applications.ResNet50(include_top=False, input_shape=img_size+(3,), pooling='avg')

# === Navigator: region proposal network (anchor-based) ===
def navigator_module(feature_map: layers.Layer):
    x = layers.Conv2D(256, 3, padding='same', activation='relu')(feature_map)
    # Predict objectness score per anchor
    obj_logits = layers.Conv2D(topN, 1)(x)
    return obj_logits

# === Teacher: score ranking loss (simplified as crossentropy guidance) ===
# We'll interpret objectness logits as teacher feedback.

# === Scrutinizer: classifier fusing global+local crops ===
def build_scrutinizer():
    inp_glob = keras.Input(shape=img_size+(3,))
    inp_crops = [keras.Input(shape=img_size+(3,)) for _ in range(topN)]
    feat_glob = base_cnn(inp_glob)
    feat_crops = [base_cnn(c) for c in inp_crops]
    all_feats = layers.Concatenate()( [feat_glob] + feat_crops )
    out = layers.Dense(1024, activation='relu')(all_feats)
    cls = layers.Dense(num_classes, activation='softmax')(out)
    return keras.Model([inp_glob]+inp_crops, cls, name='scrutinizer')

scrutinizer = build_scrutinizer()

# === Combined NTS-Net training loop ===
optimizer = keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate)
loss_fn = keras.losses.SparseCategoricalCrossentropy()

for epoch in range(epochs):
    print(f"\nEpoch {epoch+1}/{epochs}")
    for batch, (imgs, labels) in enumerate(ds_train):
        with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
            feat_map = base_cnn.get_layer(base_cnn.layers[-2].name).output
            model_extract = keras.Model(inputs=base_cnn.input, outputs=feat_map)
            fmap = model_extract(imgs, training=True)
            obj_logits = navigator_module(fmap)  # shape: (B, H, W, topN)
            # Simplify: pick topN highest score crops globally per image
            flat_logits = tf.reshape(obj_logits, [batch_size, -1, topN])
            topk_idx = tf.math.top_k(flat_logits[...,0], k=topN).indices
            # For each topk idx, turn into crop boxes (placeholder: center crop)
            crops = [tf.image.central_crop(imgs, 0.5) for _ in range(topN)]
            preds = scrutinizer([imgs]+crops, training=True)
            loss = loss_fn(labels, preds)
        grads = tape.gradient(loss, scrutinizer.trainable_variables + model_extract.trainable_variables)
        optimizer.apply_gradients(zip(grads, scrutinizer.trainable_variables + model_extract.trainable_variables))
        if batch % 50 == 0:
            print(f"Batch {batch}, Loss {float(loss):.4f}")
    # Test/metric eval here...
print("Training complete.")

Example Use Cases

Input: batch of 16 bird images (RGB tensors 224×224)
Expected Output: array of 16 softmax vectors of length 200—bird species probabilities.
